claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can improve the wear resistance of high-entropy-alloy coatings.
The proposed intervention is the introduction of a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation.
The wear-resistance improvement should hold from room temperature through 800 °C.
The nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation is the structural mediator of the intervention.
Wear resistance is improved through multi-type adaptive friction-interface protection.
The adaptive friction-interface protection is governed by intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates.
The modified coating will exhibit wear rates on the order of 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm3/Nm.
The modified coating will have lower wear than an otherwise identical unmodified high-entropy-alloy coating.
The hypothesis is bounded to temperatures at or above room temperature and at or below 800 °C.
The exact mechanism of the wear-resistance improvement is uncertain.
The optimal composition and architecture of the nanohierarchical structure are uncertain.
A comparison of coatings with and without the nanohierarchical architecture can test the hypothesis.
Wear rate, friction coefficient, and microstructure will be measured in the comparison.
Failure of the modified coating to show a significantly lower wear rate than the unmodified coating would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism field specifies a definite governing mechanism, while the uncertainty field says that the exact mechanism is uncertain.
